title: Five Mid-Atlantic gauges gave no clear change in residual monthly sea-level spread between 1980-2002 and 2003-2025
abstract: We compared residual monthly mean sea-level spread at five selected Mid-Atlantic gauges in 1980-2002 and 2003-2025. Each site and period had a separate linear trend and seasonal fit. In 2,709 accepted station-months, the equal-site mean 90th-minus-10th percentile span fell from 154.54 to 143.76 mm. The change was -10.78 mm, or -6.98%. Its conditional 95% three-year block limits were -27.72 to +21.09 mm. We thus found no clear change. Refitted year blocks kept spatial dependence. Other block lengths, a common seasonal cycle, common valid months, inferred-month inclusion and a central-span check also left the sign uncertain. This does not prove constant variability. Monthly means cannot measure storm peaks or flood risk. Selected gauges, source revisions, gaps, fitted trend removal and short-block assumptions limit inference. The package includes original code, source paths and hashes, aggregate evidence, all draws, a figure, and independent numerical and repeat checks. Raw external records remain outside the signed package.

display.caption: Residual monthly span at five gauges before and after 2003. Separate trends and seasonal means are removed. Limits use spatially paired three-year blocks and do not resolve a change.

citations.reason: The seasonal contrast study supplies prior evidence and the same five frozen NOAA sources. Our spread comparison uses overlapping data and new code.
Related monthly tail-alignment test; our endpoint is a period change in residual spread.
